sbom_standards.description: Identifies the version of the SPDX specification used to create the document. This field must appear as the first tag in an SPDX document and indicates which version of the spec the document conforms to. Without this, parsers cannot correctly interpret the document structure.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be exactly 'SPDX-2.3'. No other values are valid for SPDX 2.3 documents.

sbom_standards.description: Specifies the license under which the SPDX document data is licensed. All SPDX documents must use CC0-1.0 to ensure the SBOM metadata itself can be freely shared and consumed without license restrictions, regardless of the licenses of the software being described.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be exactly 'CC0-1.0'. This is the only valid value.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (CycloneDX does not mandate a data license)

sbom_standards.description: Uniquely identifies each element within an SPDX document. The document itself must have SPDXID 'SPDXRef-DOCUMENT'. Packages, files, and snippets each receive their own SPDXID. These identifiers are used in Relationship elements to express how components relate to each other.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must match pattern 'SPDXRef-[a-zA-Z0-9.-]+'. The document-level SPDXID must be 'SPDXRef-DOCUMENT'.

sbom_standards.description: A human-readable name for the SPDX document. This should be descriptive enough to distinguish this document from others. Common conventions include the project name and version, or the build identifier. This name is for display purposes and does not need to be globally unique.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Non-empty string. No specific format required, but should be human-readable and descriptive.

sbom_standards.description: A unique URI that provides an unambiguous identifier for this specific SPDX document. The namespace must be unique for each version of the document. It enables tools to differentiate between different SPDX documents and different versions of the same document. The URI does not need to be resolvable.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be a valid URI. Must be unique for each unique version of the SPDX document. Should not contain the '#' character.

sbom_standards.description: Identifies who or what created the SPDX document. Multiple Creator fields are allowed. Each must specify one of three types: 'Tool' for automated generators, 'Organization' for the creating organization, or 'Person' for an individual creator. At least one Creator entry is required.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be prefixed with 'Tool:', 'Organization:', or 'Person:'. At least one Creator field is required. Tool entries should include version information.
sbom_standards.examples: Tool: spdx-sbom-generator-2.0.0, Organization: Ansvar Systems AB, Person: Jane Doe (jane@example.com)

sbom_standards.description: Records the date and time when the SPDX document was created. This timestamp establishes when the SBOM was generated and is critical for determining the freshness and validity of the SBOM data. It should reflect the actual generation time, not the build time of the software.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be in ISO 8601 combined date and time format: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ. UTC timezone (Z) is required.

sbom_standards.description: The full name of the package as given by the package originator. This is the primary human-readable identifier for the package within the SBOM. For open source components, this should match the canonical name used in the package's repository or registry.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Non-empty string. Should match the canonical name of the package from its source repository or package registry.

sbom_standards.description: The version of the package. While not technically required by the spec, it is strongly recommended as version information is essential for vulnerability correlation, license compliance, and dependency resolution. Without version data, the SBOM has significantly reduced utility.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: No specific format required. Should follow the versioning convention used by the package (semver, calver, etc.).

sbom_standards.description: Identifies the actual distribution source of the package, which may differ from the originator. The supplier is the entity that provided the specific copy of the package used. This is important for supply chain traceability, as packages may be redistributed through mirrors, internal registries, or vendor channels.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be prefixed with 'Organization:' or 'Person:', or set to 'NOASSERTION' if unknown.
sbom_standards.examples: Organization: npmjs.org, Organization: Red Hat Inc., NOASSERTION

sbom_standards.description: The URI or URL from which the package can be downloaded, or a VCS location where the source can be retrieved. This field is critical for reproducibility and verification, allowing consumers to independently obtain and verify the same package. For packages from registries, this should point to the specific version.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be a valid URI, VCS URI (e.g., git+https://...), or one of the special values 'NOASSERTION' or 'NONE'.

sbom_standards.description: Indicates whether the file content of the package has been analyzed to determine file-level information such as checksums, license findings, and copyright notices. When set to false, it signals that the SBOM was generated from metadata only (e.g., package manifest) without examining actual file contents. Default is true.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be 'true' or 'false'. If false, PackageVerificationCode must be omitted. Default value is true if not specified.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (CycloneDX does not distinguish metadata-only vs. analyzed SBOMs)

sbom_standards.description: A calculated verification code derived from the SHA1 checksums of all files in the package (excluding the SPDX document itself). This provides a unique fingerprint of the package contents and enables detection of file-level tampering or modifications. It is mandatory when FilesAnalyzed is true.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be a 40-character hexadecimal SHA1 hash calculated per the SPDX algorithm. Required when FilesAnalyzed is true. Optional excluded files list may be provided.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (CycloneDX uses per-component hashes instead of a verification code)

sbom_standards.description: Provides a cryptographic hash of the package archive or distribution file. Multiple checksum entries are allowed using different algorithms. This is distinct from PackageVerificationCode in that it hashes the package artifact itself rather than its constituent files. Used to verify download integrity.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Format: 'ALGORITHM: HASH_VALUE'. Supported algorithms include SHA1, SHA256, SHA384, SHA512, MD2, MD4, MD5, MD6, BLAKE2b-256, BLAKE2b-384, BLAKE2b-512, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, ADLER32.

sbom_standards.description: The license the SPDX document creator has concluded governs the package, based on analysis of the package content, metadata, and any other relevant information. This may differ from the declared license if the actual license text found in files contradicts the declared license. Uses SPDX License Expression syntax.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be a valid SPDX license expression (e.g., 'MIT', 'Apache-2.0 OR MIT'), 'NOASSERTION', or 'NONE'. Compound expressions use AND, OR, WITH operators.
sbom_standards.examples: MIT, Apache-2.0 OR MIT, GPL-3.0-only WITH Classpath-exception-2.0, NOASSERTION

sbom_standards.description: The license declared by the package authors in their metadata (e.g., package.json, pom.xml, setup.py). This represents the license the authors intended, which may differ from the concluded license if analysis reveals discrepancies. Both declared and concluded licenses should be tracked for compliance auditing.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be a valid SPDX license expression, 'NOASSERTION', or 'NONE'. Should reflect the license field from the package's own metadata.

sbom_standards.description: The copyright holder and associated dates for the package. This field captures the copyright notices found in the package content. For compliance purposes, all unique copyright statements should be captured. If not determinable, NOASSERTION may be used.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Free-form text containing copyright statements, or 'NOASSERTION' if not determined, or 'NONE' if no copyright text exists.
sbom_standards.examples: Copyright 2024 Ansvar Systems AB, Copyright (c) 2020-2024 The Express Authors, NOASSERTION

sbom_standards.description: References an external source of information relevant to the package. The most important use case is PACKAGE-URL (purl) references, which provide a standardized way to identify packages across ecosystems. External references also support CPE identifiers for vulnerability matching and security advisory references.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Format: 'ExternalRef: CATEGORY TYPE LOCATOR'. Categories: SECURITY, PACKAGE-MANAGER, PERSISTENT-ID, OTHER. For purl: 'ExternalRef: PACKAGE-MANAGER purl pkg:npm/express@4.18.2'.
sbom_standards.examples: ExternalRef: PACKAGE-MANAGER purl pkg:npm/express@4.18.2, ExternalRef: SECURITY cpe23Type cpe:2.3:a:expressjs:express:4.18.2:*:*:*:*:node.js:*:*

sbom_standards.description: Describes how two SPDX elements relate to each other. At minimum, the document must declare a DESCRIBES relationship between the document and the top-level package. Relationships model the dependency tree, build dependencies, development tools, and other structural connections between components.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Format: 'Relationship: SPDXID RELATIONSHIP_TYPE SPDXID'. At least one 'DESCRIBES' relationship is required (SPDXRef-DOCUMENT DESCRIBES SPDXRef-Package). Valid types include: DESCRIBES, CONTAINS, DEPENDS_ON, BUILD_TOOL_OF, DEV_DEPENDENCY_OF, OPTIONAL_DEPENDENCY_OF, etc.
sbom_standards.examples: SPDXRef-DOCUMENT DESCRIBES SPDXRef-MyPackage, SPDXRef-MyPackage DEPENDS_ON SPDXRef-express, SPDXRef-MyPackage CONTAINS SPDXRef-File1

sbom_standards.description: Identifies the original author or organization that created the package. This may differ from the supplier when packages are redistributed through third-party channels. The originator is important for establishing trust chains and understanding the provenance of software components in the supply chain.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be prefixed with 'Organization:' or 'Person:', or set to 'NOASSERTION' if unknown.
sbom_standards.examples: Organization: Express.js Foundation, Person: TJ Holowaychuk, NOASSERTION

sbom_standards.description: The URL of the package's home page. This provides a reference for consumers to find documentation, release notes, and project information. While not required, it significantly improves the utility of the SBOM by allowing quick access to upstream project information during vulnerability triage.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Must be a valid URL or 'NOASSERTION' or 'NONE'.

sbom_standards.description: A detailed textual description of the package, providing context about what the software does. This supplements the PackageName by giving consumers of the SBOM meaningful context when reviewing the bill of materials, especially for components whose purpose is not obvious from the name alone.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Free-form text. No length restrictions. Should be descriptive and accurate.
sbom_standards.examples: Fast, unopinionated, minimalist web framework for Node.js

sbom_standards.description: Allows reviewers and annotators to add comments, review results, or other notes to the SPDX document or specific elements within it. Annotations include the annotator identity, date, type (REVIEW or OTHER), and comment text. This supports the review workflow for SBOM quality assurance.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Requires: Annotator (Person/Organization/Tool prefix), AnnotationDate (ISO 8601), AnnotationType (REVIEW or OTHER), AnnotationComment (free text), and SPDXID of the annotated element.
sbom_standards.examples: Annotator: Person: John Doe, AnnotationDate: 2024-06-15T14:30:00Z, AnnotationType: REVIEW, AnnotationComment: Verified license compliance for all packages
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (CycloneDX annotations are handled through metadata.properties)

sbom_standards.description: Describes a portion of a file that has different licensing, copyright, or other characteristics from the file as a whole. Snippets are identified by byte or line ranges within a file and allow granular attribution when a file contains code from multiple sources with different licenses, such as copied open source code fragments.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Requires SnippetSPDXID, SnippetFromFileSPDXID, SnippetByteRange (or SnippetLineRange), SnippetLicenseConcluded, and SnippetCopyrightText.
sbom_standards.examples: SnippetSPDXID: SPDXRef-Snippet1, SnippetFromFileSPDXID: SPDXRef-File1, SnippetByteRange: 310:420, SnippetLicenseConcluded: MIT
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: No direct equivalent (CycloneDX 1.6 does not have snippet-level granularity)
sbom_standards.keywords: snippet,code fragment,byte range,line range,partial file,license fragment

sbom_standards.description: References another SPDX document by its namespace and provides a checksum for integrity verification. This enables linking SPDX documents together to represent complex software systems where different teams or tools produce SBOMs for different subsystems. External document references make it possible to build hierarchical, multi-document SBOMs.
sbom_standards.validation_rules: Format: 'ExternalDocumentRef: DOCUMENT_REF_ID DOCUMENT_URI CHECKSUM'. The DOCUMENT_REF_ID must start with 'DocumentRef-'. A SHA1 or SHA256 checksum of the referenced document is required.
sbom_standards.equivalent_field: externalReferences with type 'bom' (CycloneDX, for linking BOMs together)
